articles.headline: Southern Powers Sign Accord Against Far Eastern Federation
articles.byline: By Our Diplomatic Correspondent · Filed From Pijao
body: A new peace accord between the Colombian Empire and China has redrawn the lines of southern politics this season, formalizing what both governments describe as a shared stance against the Far Eastern Federation rather than a conventional mutual-defense pact.

Colombian officials say the agreement was signed shortly after the Empire's independent push into South America, and represents less a promise of troops than a promise of alignment: the two powers have agreed to rally against one common target, leaving each free to conduct its own affairs elsewhere on the map.

The Federation has not issued a formal response. Its reputation on the server, however, precedes it — a leadership record that correspondents across several nations describe as having driven players to quit the game outright is cited by both Colombian and Chinese officials as the accord's underlying justification.

Colombia's existing circle of allies — Central America, the United States, and China chief among them — remains otherwise unchanged. Officials in Pijao describe the rest of the server's nations as neutral ground by default: no conflict, no treaty, simply unclaimed diplomatic territory.
The Gazette will continue to follow developments as other nations weigh whether to align, abstain, or wait the Federation's reputation out.

articles.headline: New Coastal Town of Paramaribo Joins the Empire
body: Founded just this week under Mayor OnlyADonut, Paramaribo becomes the Colombian Empire's newest settlement — its thirtieth town by the Crown's own count, and a sign the Empire's expansion shows no sign of slowing.

articles.headline: Pijao's Underground Mall Draws Traders From Across the Region
body: Beneath the Empire's coastal capital, a structured network of player shops continues to expand, with Crown officials citing it as a primary source of treasury funding — and, increasingly, a destination in its own right.

articles.headline: Salento's Sandstone Villas Reach Completion
body: Long a passion project of one of Colombia's oldest residents, Salento's distinctive sandstone architecture has become a quiet point of pride for a nation better known for its coastline than its craftsmanship.

articles.headline: Imperial Activity Law Trims Rolls, Draws Little Complaint
body: A recent enforcement of Colombia's activity requirements removed roughly a fifth of the nation's registered population. Officials say the response from citizens has been largely one of understanding rather than outrage.

articles.headline: The Gazette Is Looking For You
body: This is Issue No. 1 — and it's Colombia-heavy because that's who's written in so far. Every nation on the server has a newsroom seat waiting. Elections, wars, market reports, gossip: if it happened on DMC, it belongs here.

classifieds.text: Founding grants of 100–200 gold available to citizens establishing a new colony town. Inquire with the Crown.
By imperial edict: unused land is subject to reclamation. Build, trade, or move on.
Correspondents in every nation. The Gazette prints what its citizens send it — send yours.
